title: Patterning Bioactive Proteins or Peptides on Hydrogel Using Photochemistry for Biological Applications
protocol: Prepare stock solutions of PEGDA, LAP, and fibronectin under sterile conditions.
Weigh out compounds and dissolve them in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Dissolve PEGDA in PBS to achieve working solution concentrations between 50 and 200 mg/mL.
Pipette the PEGDA solution through a 0.22-µm syringe filter for sterilization.
Cover PEGDA solutions with foil wrapping to protect from light.
Reconstitute fibronectin protein powder based on manufacturer's recommendation.
Maintain fibronectin stock solution at 1 mg/mL concentration.
Aliquot the fibronectin stock into 60 to 100 μL portions and store at -20°C until use.
Defrost fibronectin aliquots at 4°C for several hours or overnight before use.
Sterilize protein stock with a 0.22 µm syringe filter if not provided in sterile conditions.
Weigh out LAP and dissolve it in PBS to achieve a typical stock concentration of 25 mg/mL.
Sonicate LAP solution if encountering difficulties during dissolution.
Pass the LAP solution through a 0.22 µm filter for sterilization.
Cover LAP with foil wrapping and store at 4°C for up to several months.
Prepare sterile glass slide molds for hydrogel formation.
Autoclave a polyester sheet; one is needed for each gel mold.
Soak two glass slides and three plastic spacers (0.5 mm thick) for each gel mold in 70% ethanol overnight.
Soak five binder clips for each gel mold in 70% ethanol for 10 min prior to use.
Place the glass slides, spacers, and binder clips onto a small autoclaved sheet in the cell culture hood to air dry for several hours.
Prepare hydrogel molds by placing plastic spacers around the edge of a glass slide.
Place the second glass slide on top.
Secure the spacers tightly next to each other with binder clips, two on each long side and one on top.
Surface-sterilize the mold with cell culture hood UV light for 30 min prior to use.
Flip the mold halfway through to expose both surfaces.
Adjust PBS to pH 8 and add 5 mM EDTA to prepare reaction buffer.
Pipette reaction buffer into a 0.22 μm syringe filter for sterilization.
Weigh out 2-iminothiolane and dissolve it in reaction buffer for a concentration of 2 mg/mL (14 mM).
Pass the solution through a 0.22-µm syringe filter for sterilization.
Store the stock solution at 4 °C.
Reconstitute the protein in reaction buffer at a concentration between 0.1 and 1 mg/mL unless previously sterile.
Pipette the reconstituted protein solution through a 0.22-µm syringe filter for sterilization.
Mix the protein with 2-iminothiolane using a molar ratio of 8:1.
Incubate the reaction for 1 h at room temperature.
Use a desalting spin micro-column to remove the thiolated protein product from remaining reactants.
Follow the manufacturer's protocol for Ellman's Assay to measure free thiols per protein quantitatively.
Create the gel precursor solution based on values calculated from Table 1C.
Mix together the PEGDA, fibronectin, and LAP volumes.
Pipette the solution vigorously to ensure a homogenous solution without creating bubbles.
Keep the solution protected from light.
Pipette the gel precursor solution carefully between two glass slides of the gel mold.
Add a volume between 800 and 1,000 µL to the mold.
Expose the gel solution in the mold to UV light (wavelength: 365 nm, power: 3-4 mW/cm2) for 1-2 min to form the hydrogel.
Do not expose the hydrogel to prolonged UV light.
Remove the binder clips and gently remove top glass slide by applying opposite pressure to the two side spacers.
Use an appropriately sized biopsy punch to cut out the hydrogel samples.
Punch out multiple hydrogels from the gel rectangle for replicates and control samples.
Punch out hydrogels with an 8 mm-diameter biopsy punch for an 8 mm parallel plate rheometer.
Load one hydrogel sample into the rheometer.
Lower the parallel plate geometry that is 8 mm in diameter until making contact with the surface of the gel.
Keep a gap distance of 0.5 mm for a 0.5 mm-thick hydrogel sample.
Perform time sweeps for 5 min at 0.1% strain, 0.1 Hz frequency, and 37 °C.
Average the G' values across each time sweep.
Run independent hydrogels for replicates of each composition.
Prepare the desired pattern for the photomask using a computer aided design (CAD) program.
Print the photomask on a transparent sheet using a high-resolution printer.
Soak the photomask in 70% ethanol for 10 min prior to use.
Allow the photomask to air dry in a cell culture hood before use.
Add the thiolated protein solution prepared in step 2 to the surface of the hydrogel for surface patterning.
Pipette 1-2 µL/cm² of thiolated protein solution to the surface of each cut-out gel.
Carefully place the photomask on the surface of the hydrogel.
Do not allow air bubbles between the photomask and the hydrogel surface.
Gently press down on the mask to remove any bubbles that form.
Expose the hydrogel to a second round of UV light (wavelength: 365 nm, power: 3-4 mW/cm²) for 30-60 s.
Wash hydrogels with PBS to remove unreacted species and place each hydrogel within the well plate with patterned surface face up.
Incubate gels in basal medium for 5-10 min at 37°C prior to seeding.
For human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs), use EGM-2 medium without growth factors.
Minimize the volume of medium added to each well to prevent hydrogel floating.
Spin down the plate at 300 x g for 3 min to ensure that the hydrogels are located at the bottom of the well and are not floating.
Use standard sterile mammalian cell culture procedures for cell seeding and experimental procedures.
Remove HUVECs from tissue culture flasks using standard cell detachment protocols.
Wash the tissue culture dish with sterile PBS and incubate with trypsin for 3-5 min at 37°C.
Quench the trypsinized cell suspension with excess cell medium or trypsin neutralizer solution.
Spin down the cell suspension in the centrifuge at 300 x g for 5 min.
Carefully remove the supernatant and keep the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in basal EGM-2 with no growth factors.
Use a hemocytometer for cell counting.
Add 75,000 cells/cm² to each hydrogel surface by pipetting slowly into the center of each well.
Place the well plate into a cell culture incubator at 37 °C.
Remove the dish periodically for observation over several days.
Culture E. coli overnight in suspension in LB broth in an orbital shaker at 37 °C and 200 rpm.
Spin down the E. coli culture, decant, and reconstitute the cell pellet in minimal volume of PBS.
Weigh out the lysozyme and reconstitute at 1 mg/mL for the stock solution.
Pipette a small volume (25 µL) of lysozyme stock solution into microcentrifuge tubes.
Add varying levels of LAP photoinitiator (0-12 mM).
Expose the samples to 1 min of UV light.
In a separate group, add 2 mM LAP to the lysozyme solution and expose samples to varying UV light times (0-4 min).
Include replicates for each treatment.
Add equal volume of concentrated E. coli solution to each lysozyme sample for a final lysozyme protein concentration of 0.5 mg/mL.
Incubate the mixed solutions for 4 h at room temperature.
Use untreated lysozyme incubated with E. coli as a positive control.
Incubate lysozyme solution with PBS alone for a negative control.
Spin down samples to remove cell debris and retain the supernatant.
Run a Bradford assay on the supernatant to quantify total protein concentration.
Follow the manufacturer's protocol for conducting the Bradford assay.
Calculate the fold change in protein concentration relative to the negative control.
